mainTopic: The meaning of the משנה's case of slaughtering the קרבן פסח both לשמו and שלא לשמו: does it refer to one עבודה or two עבודות, and how does this fit רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי?
overview: The גמרא asks whether the משנה's case of a פסח slaughtered with mixed intentions, לשמו ושלא לשמו, happened within one עבודה, which would fit only רבי יוסי, or across two עבודות, which even רבי מאיר would disqualify. It first explains that the question only matters when the good intention comes first. It then tries several proofs that the משנה means one עבודה. First it rereads the משנה's list of slaughter, receiving, carrying and sprinkling as alternative cases, and argues that the סיפא must then be one עבודה so it does not repeat the רישא. That proof is rejected: the סיפא can teach that one may have intention during one עבודה about another, which is the issue רב פפא asked about. A proof from the case שלא לשמו ולשמו is rejected as something the משנה added only to match the case before it. A proof from the next משנה about slaughtering for the wrong eaters is rejected because the two משניות need not match. Finally the גמרא brings the ruling that slaughtering for eaters and non-eaters is כשר. It shows that a two-עבודות reading of that ruling clashes with the rule מקצת אוכלין לא פסלא, and the argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The second option: maybe the משנה means two different services
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the other side of its question. Maybe the משנה is talking about two separate עבודות, and in that case even רבי מאיר agrees the offering is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps the משנה is teaching about two services. Even רבי מאיר, who says we hold a person to his first words, only says that within one service. With two services, he agrees the offering becomes disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a two-sided question that started on the previous amud. Here it offers the second possibility: the two intentions were spoken during two different עבודות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר usually says only a person's first words count (תפוס לשון ראשון). That rule applies when both statements are made within one עבודה. If the second intention is attached to a separate עבודה, it stands on its own, so even רבי מאיר agrees it disqualifies.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. This introduces the second side of a question.
A service or rite in the קרבן process, such as slaughtering, receiving, carrying or sprinkling.
Hold onto the first expression. Only a person's first words count. This is רבי מאיר's view.
He agrees or concedes.
It becomes disqualified (פסול).

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the second half of a question that began on the previous amud. The first half was that the משנה means one עבודה and follows רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is in two services that we learned (the case of the Mishnah),
and even according to Rabbi Meir,
who said 'hold onto the first expression' —
these words apply only in one service,
but in two services —
he agrees that it becomes disqualified.
phrases.notes: The second intention belongs to a separate service, so it counts on its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second side of the question begun on the previous amud (one עבודה versus two עבודות).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the משנה's mixed-intention case happen within one עבודה (only רבי יוסי) or across two עבודות (everyone, even רבי מאיר)?

steps.title: Which order of intentions is the question about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case of the משנה the question refers to. It rules out the order 'not for its own purpose, then for its own purpose,' because that case is disqualified according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: which case is this about? If you say it is about 'not for its own purpose, then for its own purpose,' then it does not matter whether it was one service or two, or whether we follow רבי מאיר or רבי יוסי. The offering was already disqualified by the first statement. For רבי יוסי also holds that a person is held 'even' by the end of his words, meaning his first words count too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask exactly which case its question is about. It shows that one possible order cannot be what the question means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wrong intention (שלא לשמו) comes first, רבי מאיר disqualifies the offering because the first words count. רבי יוסי also holds that both the beginning and the end of a statement count, so the bad first words still count for him. In this order the offering is פסול for everyone, so there is nothing to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: On which one? Which case is being discussed?
Not for its own purpose, meaning with the wrong intention.
From the first one, meaning from the first statement.
A person is held to the end of his words as well. This is רבי יוסי's view.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי does not say that only the last words count. He says the last words also count, together with the first words. So a bad first statement still disqualifies the offering according to him.

phrases.english: They said: On which (case) is this?
If we say it is on 'not for its own purpose and for its own purpose,'

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בַּעֲבוֹדָה אַחַת בֵּין בִּשְׁתֵּי עֲבוֹדוֹת,
phrases.english: whether in one service or in two services,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר בֵּין לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי —
phrases.english: whether according to Rabbi Meir or according to Rabbi Yosei —
it was disqualified from the first (statement),
for according to Rabbi Yosei too,

phrases.aramaic: אַף בִּגְמַר דְּבָרָיו אָדָם נִתְפָּס אִית לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: he holds that a person is held even by the conclusion of his words (in addition to the beginning).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question from step 1 by ruling out one order of intentions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which order of intentions in the משנה is the one-עבודה versus two-עבודות question about?

steps.title: The question is about 'for its own purpose, then not for its own purpose'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the question must be about the opposite order: first לשמו, then שלא לשמו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question is about 'for its own purpose, then not for its own purpose.' What is the case there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles which case its question really refers to. It then asks again: in that case, is it one עבודה or two?
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the good intention comes first, רבי מאיר would ignore the bad second statement if both were said within one עבודה. So the only real disagreement is in this order. Here the difference between one עבודה and two matters.

keyTerms.meaning: For its own purpose, meaning with the correct intention for this קרבן.
What? What is the case?

steps.whatToRemember: The one-עבודה versus two-עבודות question only matters when the good intention comes first and the bad intention second (לשמו ושלא לשמו).

phrases.english: Rather: on 'for its own purpose and not for its own purpose' — what (is the case)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the clarification in step 2 and restates the main question in its proper case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question is about לשמו ושלא לשמו, where רבי מאיר's first-words rule could make a difference.

steps.title: A source is brought: the משנה's list of four services
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a proof by quoting the משנה about a פסח that was slaughtered, and its blood received, carried and sprinkled, all שלא לשמו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a פסח that was slaughtered not for its own purpose, and its blood was received, carried and sprinkled not for its own purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to try to answer the question. This step only quotes the text and prepares the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted line lists four separate עבודות. The גמרא will look closely at why the משנה needs to mention all four. That close reading is what will answer the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering the animal.
He received the blood in a vessel.
He carried the blood to the מזבח.
He sprinkled the blood on the מזבח.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A Paschal lamb that one slaughtered not for its own purpose,
and received, and carried, and sprinkled (the blood) not for its own purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question from step 3.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the סיפא's לשמו ושלא לשמו refers to one עבודה, following רבי יוסי. The proof works by first defining what the רישא covers.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing slaughter, receiving, carrying and sprinkling שלא לשמו.

steps.title: Why would the משנה need to list all four services?
steps.stepSummary: Read literally, the list is unnecessary. The bad intention at the slaughter already disqualifies the offering, so why mention all four services?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If it is exactly as written, why must he have the wrong intention for all of them? The offering was already disqualified by the first one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the plain reading of the quoted משנה. If every service was done with the wrong intention, mentioning the later ones adds nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wrong intention at the slaughter alone is enough to make the פסח invalid. So listing receiving, carrying and sprinkling seems pointless. This forces the גמרא to look for a different reading.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How is it set up?
As it is taught, meaning the literal reading.
Why do I need this? Why is it written?
He has an intention (מחשבה).

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say it is as it is taught (literally),
why do I need that he has (wrong) intent for all of them?
It was already disqualified from the first one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the literal reading of the source just quoted, to set up the proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal reading of the משנה, in which all four עבודות were שלא לשמו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first bad intention at the slaughter already disqualifies the offering, so the rest of the list would be extra words.

steps.title: Reading the משנה as different cases shows it means two services
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the רישא of the משנה as a list of alternative cases. In each one, the good intention comes in earlier services and the bad intention comes in a later service. So the רישא already covers לשמו followed by שלא לשמו across two עבודות. The next step uses this to argue about the סיפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not teaching this: a פסח slaughtered not for its own purpose; or slaughtered for its own purpose but the blood was received, carried and sprinkled not for its own purpose; or slaughtered, received and carried for its own purpose but sprinkled not for its own purpose. That is a case of two services.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own challenge by reading the list as separate options instead of one case. This shows that the רישא is a two-עבודות case, which sets up the argument about the סיפא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each option has the correct intention in early services and the wrong intention in a later, different service. So the רישא already teaches לשמו followed by שלא לשמו spread over two עבודות, a case even רבי מאיר agrees is פסול. The סיפא's separate words "לשמו ושלא לשמו" must then teach something else, as the next step argues.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that... This introduces the proposed correct reading.
This is what it teaches, meaning a rereading of the text.
Or alternatively.

steps.whatToRemember: The רישא's list of four services is read as separate options, each moving from לשמו to שלא לשמו in a later service. So the רישא already covers the two-עבודות case, which even רבי מאיר agrees is פסול. The next step uses this reading to argue that the סיפא must then be about one עבודה.
steps.confusionAlert: The words 'and received, and carried, and sprinkled' are not one single case. The גמרא reads them as a list of different options.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading lets the רישא fit רבי מאיר as well. It also becomes the basis for the next step's claim that the סיפא, if read as two עבודות, would only repeat the רישא.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that this is what it teaches:
A Paschal lamb that one slaughtered not for its own purpose,
or alternatively, he slaughtered it for its own purpose
and received, carried, and sprinkled not for its own purpose;

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי שְׁחָטוֹ וְקִבֵּל וְהִלֵּךְ לִשְׁמוֹ,
phrases.english: or alternatively, he slaughtered, received, and carried for its own purpose,
and sprinkled not for its own purpose.
So it is a case of two services.
phrases.notes: Here's the proof: in the משנה, the mixed intentions are each on a different service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 5 by rereading the source, which produces the proof for step 3's question.
steps.raayaObject: That the רישא already covers לשמו followed by שלא לשמו in two עבודות. This is the setup for proving that the סיפא is one עבודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's list of four services, reread as alternative cases.

steps.title: The סיפא must be about one service, following רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that the סיפא's "לשמו ושלא לשמו" cannot mean two עבודות, because that would just repeat the רישא. So it must mean one עבודה, following רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the later clause of the משנה: "for its own sake and not for its own sake." What case is this? If it means two services, that is the same as the first clause! So it must mean one service, and it follows רבי יוסי, who said a person is held to the end of his words too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds on the proof it just made from the רישא. It now looks at the סיפא of the same משנה to try to settle the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 showed that the רישא already covers good intention in an earlier עבודה and bad intention in a later one. If the סיפא meant the same thing, it would be a pointless repeat. So the סיפא must mean someone who said both intentions during one עבודה. It is פסול because, according to רבי יוסי, the second half of a statement also counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (look at) the later clause of the משנה
What is the case? How do we picture it?
That is the same as the first clause
During a single service
A person is held accountable even for the end of his statement (רבי יוסי)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the רישא and the סיפא. Here, רישא means the four-service list (שחטו, קבל, הלך, זרק). סיפא means the later words "לשמו ושלא לשמו" and "שלא לשמו ולשמו."
steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof holds, the משנה would answer the open question: mixed intention within one עבודה disqualifies, following רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
for its own sake and not for its own sake,
what are the circumstances?
If we say it is during two services,
that is the same as the first clause!
Rather, is it not during one service,
and it follows Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אַף בִּגְמַר דְּבָרָיו אָדָם נִתְפָּס.
phrases.english: who said: a person is held accountable even for the end of his words.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא סֵיפָא: לִשְׁמוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ, הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 6 (the רישא covers two עבודות) to force a one-עבודה reading of the סיפא.
steps.raayaObject: That "לשמו ושלא לשמו" within one עבודה disqualifies the פסח
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה, read as non-repetitive of the רישא, explained according to רבי יוסי

steps.title: Both clauses can be two services: the רישא is about thinking on the same service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. It explains that the רישא is a case where the כהן is doing a service and has bad intention about that same service.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really both clauses are about two services. The first clause is where he is standing at the slaughter and thinking about the slaughter. Or he is standing at the sprinkling and thinking about the sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 7. It starts by redefining the רישא so that the סיפא can still be about two עבודות without repeating it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 7 assumed that "two עבודות" can only mean one thing. The דחיה shows that there are two kinds of two-service cases. In the רישא, the bad thought is about the very service being done right now.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (keeping the original reading)
He is standing at (is in the middle of doing)
Has an intention, thinks (in the halachic sense of מחשבה)
Slaughtering the animal
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: No, really it is during two services,
and the first clause is where he stands at the slaughter
and thinks about the slaughter,
or alternatively, he stands at the sprinkling
and thinks about the sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 7 by redefining what the רישא covers.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the סיפא must be about one עבודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed a two-עבודות reading of the סיפא must repeat the רישא. But the רישא can be limited to intention about the service currently being done.

steps.title: The סיפא teaches intention from one service about another, which is רב פפא's question
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא is a case where the כהן is slaughtering but has bad intention about the later sprinkling. This teaches that one can have intention from one עבודה about another, which is exactly רב פפא's question.
steps.simpleTranslation: The later clause is where he stands at the slaughter and thinks about the sprinkling. He says: "I am slaughtering the פסח for its own sake, in order to sprinkle its blood not for its own sake." And the משנה teaches us that one can have intention from one service to another. This is the question of רב פפא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its rejection by explaining the סיפא as a different kind of two-service case. So the סיפא is not a repeat, and it says nothing about one עבודה or רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סיפא, the actual שחיטה is לשמו, but during it the כהן plans a שלא לשמו זריקה. The new point is that a thought during one service about a later service can disqualify the offering, which is the very issue רב פפא asked about. Because the סיפא has its own new point, it does not need to be about one עבודה, so our original question is still not settled.

keyTerms.meaning: I hereby (am doing)
It teaches us (the new point is)
One can have intention during one service about a different service
The open question asked by רב פפא

steps.whatToRemember: Two kinds of two-service cases: (1) the רישא, where the bad thought is about the service you are doing now; (2) the סיפא, where during the שחיטה you plan a bad זריקה ("מחשבין מעבודה לעבודה"). Because of this, the proof from "לשמו ושלא לשמו" fails.
steps.confusionAlert: In the סיפא case, the שחיטה itself really is לשמו. The bad intention is about the future זריקה, not about the slaughter being done now.

phrases.english: The latter clause is where he stands at the slaughter
and thinks about the sprinkling,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: הֲרֵינִי שׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַפֶּסַח לִשְׁמוֹ
phrases.english: for he said: I am hereby slaughtering the Paschal offering for its own sake
to sprinkle its blood not for its own sake.
And it teaches us
that one can intend from one service to another service,
and this is the question of Rav Pappa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the דחיה of step 8 by giving the סיפא its own two-עבודות case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the סיפא's "לשמו ושלא לשמו"
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The סיפא has its own new point (intention from one עבודה to another), so it does not need to be about one עבודה or follow רבי יוסי.

steps.title: New proof opened from "not for its own sake and then for its own sake"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new proof from the last case in the משנה: שלא לשמו ולשמו is פסול. It asks what case this is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: "or not for its own sake and then for its own sake, it is disqualified." What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes another phrase of the משנה and asks what case it describes, preparing the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from "לשמו ושלא לשמו" was pushed away, so the גמרא tries the opposite order. The question "היכי דמי" sets up the same method as before: test whether a two-עבודות reading makes the clause unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualified

phrases.english: Come and hear:
or not for its own sake and for its own sake, it is disqualified.
What are the circumstances?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ וְלִשְׁמוֹ פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in steps 7 to 9 failed, opens a fresh proof from the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That mixed intention within one עבודה disqualifies (to be developed)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The final clause of the משנה: "או שלא לשמו ולשמו פסול"

steps.title: Read as two services, the clause would be obvious
steps.stepSummary: If "שלא לשמו ולשמו" meant two עבודות, it would be obvious. Since "לשמו ושלא לשמו" is already פסול, the case where the bad intention comes first is surely פסול too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we say it is during two services: now that you said "for its own sake and then not for its own sake" is disqualified, do you even need to say "not for its own sake and then for its own sake"?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the two-services reading of this clause and shows that it makes the clause unnecessary. This prepares the conclusion in the next step (step 12) that it must be talking about one עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bad intention comes in the first service, the offering is already ruined right away. That is even more obvious than when the bad intention comes later. So the משנה would not bother to teach it, which pushes toward a one-עבודה reading.

keyTerms.meaning: If we say (testing a possible reading)
Now that (introducing a "how much more so" argument)
Is it even necessary to say? (it is obvious)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the end of the proof. The גמרא is only ruling out the two-עבודות reading here, and the conclusion comes in step 12 of the סוגיא.

phrases.english: If we say it is during two services,

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא לִשְׁמוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ אָמְרַתְּ פָּסוּל,
phrases.english: now that you said for its own sake and not for its own sake is disqualified,
is it necessary to say not for its own sake and for its own sake?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נֵימָא בִּשְׁתֵּי עֲבוֹדוֹת, הַשְׁתָּא לִשְׁמוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ אָמְרַתְּ פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the "היכי דמי" of step 10 by eliminating the two-עבודות option.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading "שלא לשמו ולשמו" in the משנה as two עבודות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: if a bad intention in a later עבודה disqualifies, then a bad intention in the earlier עבודה surely disqualifies. So the clause would be redundant.

steps.title: So the last case must be one service, and the first case too
steps.stepSummary: Since שלא לשמו ולשמו cannot mean two עבודות, it must mean one עבודה. By the same pattern, the earlier case לשמו ושלא לשמו also means one עבודה, following רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it talking about one service? And since the last case is about one service, the first case is also about one service!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof it began in step 10. The last case must be about one עבודה, so the earlier case must be too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 showed that reading the last case as two עבודות would make it obvious. So the last case must mean one עבודה. The גמרא assumes the clauses of a משנה work the same way, so the earlier case is also one עבודה, which fits רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it…? (a phrase that pushes toward the only remaining reading)
One service, such as only the שחיטה
And since the later clause…
The first clause also

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it about one service?
phrases.notes: Because if it were two services, that would be obvious, as we saw in step 11.

phrases.english: And since the last clause is about one service —
phrases.notes: The last clause is שלא לשמו ולשמו.

phrases.english: the first clause is also about one service!
phrases.notes: The first clause is לשמו ושלא לשמו, which would follow רבי יוסי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof that step 11's difficulty made possible.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's case of לשמו ושלא לשמו is about one עבודה, following רבי יוסי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The last case of the משנה (שלא לשמו ולשמו), together with the idea that the clauses of a משנה run in parallel.

steps.title: The last case is really two services, taught only to match
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the last case really is two עבודות. It was not truly needed, but the משנה added it to match the earlier case.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, really it is about two services. By right it was not needed. But since the משנה taught 'for its purpose and not for its purpose,' it also taught 'not for its purpose and for its purpose.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 12. It admits the last case is obvious, but says the משנה included it only for style.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof relied on the idea that a משנה never teaches something obvious. The answer is that sometimes a משנה adds an obvious case only because it matches the case before it. So the last case can be two עבודות, and nothing proves the earlier case is one עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / in truth (keeping the original reading)
Two services, such as שחיטה and זריקה
By right / strictly speaking
Since it taught (this), it also taught (that)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the last case is wrong or useless as a law. It agrees the case is obvious. It only explains why the משנה bothered to write it.

phrases.english: No, really it is about two services,
phrases.notes: The גמרא sticks with the very reading the proof tried to rule out.

phrases.english: and by right it was not needed,
phrases.notes: The גמרא admits that case really is obvious.

phrases.english: but since it taught 'for its purpose and not for its purpose,'
it also taught 'not for its purpose and for its purpose.'
phrases.notes: The reverse order was added to keep the pattern.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the last case of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed a משנה never includes an obvious case. In fact, a משנה can include one to match a parallel case (אגב).

steps.title: A new proof from the next משנה about the wrong eaters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the next משנה: if he slaughtered the פסח for people who cannot eat it, who are not registered, or who are ערלים or טמאים, it is פסול. That case is clearly one עבודה, so our משנה should be one עבודה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If he slaughtered it for people who cannot eat it, for people not registered for it, or for uncircumcised or impure people, it is invalid. Here it is obviously one service. And since the later משנה is about one service, the earlier one is also about one service!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second proof. It points to the next משנה, where the bad intention clearly happens during the slaughtering itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the next משנה, the כהן is slaughtering and thinking about the wrong eaters, so everything happens within one עבודה. The גמרא treats that משנה as the 'סיפא' of ours and argues that both should deal with the same kind of case. If so, our משנה is also about one עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: For people who cannot eat it
Those registered in advance for this קרבן פסח
Uncircumcised and ritually impure people, who may not eat the פסח
It is obvious

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he slaughtered it for people who cannot eat it,
phrases.notes: For example, sick or elderly people who cannot eat a כזית.

phrases.english: or for people not registered for it,
or for uncircumcised or impure people — it is invalid.
Here it is obviously about one service,
phrases.notes: The intention is held during the שחיטה itself.

phrases.english: and since the later clause is about one service —
phrases.notes: The 'later clause' here is the next משנה.

phrases.english: the earlier clause is also about one service!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה deals with one עבודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The next משנה (שחטו שלא לאוכליו), which clearly deals with one עבודה.

steps.title: The two משניות do not have to match
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Each משנה stands as it is: the next משנה is one עבודה, while ours could be either one עבודה or two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these comparable?! This one is as it is, and that one is as it is. The later משנה is about one service. The earlier one could be about one service or about two services.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says there is no reason to force the two משניות into the same kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed our משנה must follow the pattern of the next one. The גמרא answers that each משנה can have its own setup. So our משנה may still be about two עבודות, and the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this comparable?! (rejects a forced parallel)
This one is as it is, and that one is as it is
Either… or…

steps.whatToRemember: Every proof so far that our משנה deals with one עבודה (following רבי יוסי) has been rejected: the סיפא (steps 7–9), the last case שלא לשמו ולשמו (steps 10–13), and the next משנה (steps 14–15). Our משנה can still be read as two עבודות, so the question is not yet settled. Step 16 tries another proof.

phrases.english: Are these comparable?!
This one is as it is, and that one is as it is:
the later משנה is about one service,
the earlier one is either about one service,
or about two services.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי אִירְיָא? הָא כִּדְאִיתָא וְהָא כִּדְאִיתָא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the next משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed neighboring משניות must deal with the same kind of case, but each can stand on its own.

steps.title: A new proof: for eaters and non-eaters is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new proof from the next משנה, which rules that slaughtering the פסח for those who can eat it and for those who cannot is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if he slaughtered it for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new proof by quoting a line from the next משנה. This step only sets up the proof. The next steps will analyze what the line means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last proof in Step 14 was rejected in Step 15. Now the גמרא tries a different line from the same משנה. Here the mixed thought (fit eaters plus unfit eaters) is ruled כשר, and the גמרא will try to show that this only makes sense as one עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: For its eaters: people who are able and registered to eat the פסח
For those who are not its eaters: people who cannot eat it or are not registered
Valid

phrases.english: Come and hear:
For its eaters and for those who are not its eaters, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 15 rejected the first proof from the next משנה, this step brings a second line from that same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה (לשמו ושלא לשמו) speaks about one עבודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The next משנה: לְאוֹכְלָיו וְשֶׁלֹּא לְאוֹכְלָיו כָּשֵׁר

steps.title: What exactly is the case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the circumstances of the ruling are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case the ruling is talking about. This sets up the next step, where it will test one possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling could be about two separate thoughts during two different עבודות, or about one mixed thought during one עבודה. The proof depends on which reading is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? A request to define the exact case

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact case of the source quoted in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ruling is about two עבודות or one עבודה

steps.title: Testing the reading of two separate rites
steps.stepSummary: Suppose it means two עבודות. Then the reason it is כשר is that the bad thought was during זריקה, and thoughts about eaters do not matter during זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we say it means two rites, then the reason it is valid is that he had the bad thought during the sprinkling, because a thought about eaters does not count during the sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out the first possible answer: the case is two עבודות. He slaughtered for the fit eaters and did the זריקה for the unfit ones. This answer is only being tested, and the next step will show its problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thought about who will eat the קרבן only counts during שחיטה, not during זריקה. So if the bad thought came during זריקה, that alone would explain why it is כשר. The rest of the argument builds on this explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: If we say: introduces a possible reading that is being tested
Two different rites, for example שחיטה and זריקה
Throwing the blood onto the מזבח
A thought about who will eat the קרבן

phrases.english: If we say it means during two rites,
then the reason is that he had the thought during the sprinkling,
phrases.notes: That is, the bad thought about non-eaters.

phrases.english: because a thought about eaters does not count during the sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the first possible answer to the question of Step 17, so that it can be tested.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A trial reading: two עבודות, where the bad thought came during זריקה

steps.title: The two-rite reading clashes with a known rule
steps.stepSummary: If it is two עבודות, the hidden implication is that the same mixed thought during one עבודה, like שחיטה, would be פסול. But we already know that some unfit eaters do not make the קרבן פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: That implies that during one rite, such as the slaughtering, where a thought about eaters does count, it would be invalid. But we hold that some unfit eaters do not invalidate it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the problem with the two-rite reading. That reading would mean a mixed thought during שחיטה makes the קרבן פסול, but that goes against a rule we already know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only reason for כשר were that the thought came during זריקה, then the same thought during שחיטה would make it פסול. But the rule is מִקְצָת אוֹכְלִין לָא פָּסְלָא: when only some of the intended eaters are unfit, the קרבן stays valid. So the two-rite reading does not work, and the גמרא is pushing toward reading the case as one עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: One rite
Slaughtering, the rite where a thought about eaters does count
But we hold: introduces a known rule that contradicts the current reading
When only some of the eaters are unfit, it does not invalidate the קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying a mixed thought during שחיטה really is פסול. That is only the unwanted result of the two-rite reading, and the גמרא rejects it because of the known rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the next move. Since the two-rite reading fails, the ruling must be about one עבודה, and that becomes the basis for proving how to read our משנה.

phrases.english: That implies that during one rite,

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן בִּשְׁחִיטָה דְּמַהְנְיָא בַּיהּ מַחְשְׁבֶת אוֹכְלִין — פָּסוּל,
phrases.english: such as the slaughtering, where a thought about eaters does count, it would be invalid,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא קַיְימָא לַן מִקְצָת אוֹכְלִין לָא פָּסְלָא!
phrases.english: but we hold that some unfit eaters do not invalidate it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קַיְימָא לַן מִקְצָת אוֹכְלִין לָא פָּסְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what the two-rite reading of Step 18 would imply and shows that the implication contradicts a known rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that לְאוֹכְלָיו וְשֶׁלֹּא לְאוֹכְלָיו means two עבודות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading implies a mixed thought during שחיטה is פסול, but מִקְצָת אוֹכְלִין לָא פָּסְלָא says it is כשר.
